metric.definition: Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators.

reading.body:
Equipment lead times—the delay from order to installation for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling systems, and accelerators—have become as constraining on data center construction as permitting itself.

These times stretched from months to years as demand for AI infrastructure outpaced manufacturing capacity. Transformers and switchgear, the electrical backbone of any data center, now sit in queues longer than the construction schedules that depend on them. This is not a temporary bottleneck. It reflects the hard reality that power infrastructure components cannot be expedited the way software can, and that the factories producing them cannot scale as quickly as hyperscalers can spend.

For AI, this matters directly. Compute requires buildings, buildings require power infrastructure, and power infrastructure requires lead times that now determine when clusters come online. A data center that breaks ground in month one might sit idle for months after construction because the transformer needed for energization is still in a queue. The constraint has shifted from whether you can build to whether you can equip. Financing, real estate, and permitting remain critical, but they no longer gate the timeline alone.

This metric does not measure actual lead times in days or weeks. It flags where to find them, pointing to industry surveys and research firms that track market data. The direction and magnitude of the shift matter more than a single snapshot.
